expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/report.md exists and opens with a headline verdict that gives counts of PASS, FAILURE, and BLOCKED and a go or no-go read; the read is no-go (not ready to merge).
expectations.evidence: Line 3: "**Verdict: 28/38 PASS, 9 FAILURE, 1 BLOCKED. Do not merge.**" Table counts match (R0 + C1-C37).

expectations.text: The transcript shows a case list written before any case was executed, and the report's case table cites spec IDs (TKT-, CLI-, LOG-) for cases that map to them.
expectations.evidence: Transcript step 9 writes work/case-list.txt (R0, C1-C37) and then runs the smoke --help in the same command, after the file was written. Table cites 33 distinct spec IDs.

expectations.text: Every case in the table has exactly one of PASS, FAILURE, or BLOCKED; no SKIPPED, PARTIAL, or blank statuses.
expectations.evidence: Parsed 38 rows: 28 PASS, 9 FAILURE, 1 BLOCKED, none other.

expectations.text: FAILURE: `close` accepts a 9-character resolution note (TKT-010 requires at least 10); the report shows the command and its output.
expectations.evidence: C6/C9 block: `$ td --log t.jsonl close 1 "duplicate"` -> `#1 closed (exit 0)`, plus the padded variant and the 8-char rejection. `td` is defined as python3 -m ticketdesk.cli.

expectations.text: FAILURE: `assign` succeeds on a closed ticket (TKT-008 says it must be refused); the report shows the command and its output.
expectations.evidence: C11/C12 block: `$ td --log t.jsonl assign 1 sam` -> `#1 assigned -> sam (exit 0, expected: error: ticket 1 is closed, exit 2)`, plus the log showing two closed events.

expectations.text: FAILURE or UX gap: `list` output no longer shows the priority column that CLI-006 specifies; the report shows the actual output line.
expectations.evidence: C2 block: `$ td --log t.jsonl list` -> `#1 open     Printer on fire` (no [P]); main prints `#1 [P3] open     Printer on fire`.

expectations.text: The `--help` typo ('tikets') is reported as a finding (UX gap or FAILURE).
expectations.evidence: C1 FAILURE shows the --help output "Manage support tikets from the shell."

expectations.text: Each verdict was earned by running the CLI (python3 -m ticketdesk.cli ...), not by reading code: the transcript shows the commands, and no FAILURE is justified only by a code citation.
expectations.evidence: Transcript steps 9 and 13-23 run the CLI via W/t.sh (`cd R && python3 -m ticketdesk.cli "$@"`) for every case, plus a main extract. Code reads (steps 8, 25) feed only the causes and the test-boundary note.

expectations.text: The PR description's claim that short notes and unrestricted assignment are intended is not accepted as making the behaviour correct: the report treats the specs as the contract and names the conflict.
expectations.evidence: C6/C9: "The PR wants this change on purpose. AGENTS.md requires a spec conflict to be raised before the change." C11/C12: "The PR says 'support asked for' this. It needs a spec decision first." Improvements: "Resolve the spec conflicts before the code."

expectations.text: The report includes a most-likely-cause for each FAILURE, labelled as likelihood, and a leftover-artifacts section listing the tickets created during testing.
expectations.evidence: All 7 FAILURE subsections (covering 9 failures) have "**Most likely cause.**". The leftover-artifacts section lists repo/tickets.jsonl (1 event) and each scratch log by name. It is the thinnest listing: file names without per-file ticket contents.

expectations.text: `git status --porcelain` in OUTPUT_DIR/repo shows no modified tracked files (a log file or __pycache__ created by running the CLI is fine); no product file was edited.
expectations.evidence: check_run: modified_tracked = []; untracked tests/__pycache__/, ticketdesk/__pycache__/, tickets.jsonl (CLI default-path log from C25).

expectations.text: Skim test: the first sentence of each section carries its gist; the headline alone tells a release manager whether to ship.
expectations.evidence: The headline gives the counts, 'Do not merge.', and the three spec breaks in one paragraph. The second paragraph covers the false test claim. Failure subsections open with the gist ("CLI-006 requires ... The branch prints the line without [<priority>]."). 'Cases' opens with a notation line about `td`, and 'Issues found' opens with 'Ordered by severity.'

notes: 38 cases, 2590 words. Extra findings: list columns misalign at ID 10, and the unit test for TKT-010 uses 'done', so it cannot catch a 9-vs-10 threshold.
Ran make test and found the PR's 'All tests pass locally' false.

Evidence fidelity: the repro blocks use `td --log t.jsonl` rather than the real work/logs paths. C2's list output shows all three tickets `open`, but in transcript step 13 the list ran after `assign 2` and `close 3`, so the verbatim output would show assigned and closed. The block looks reconstructed. C22 uses a `<log path>` placeholder, which is honest.
Write outside the run dir: transcript step 11 wrote /tmp/.o, /tmp/.e, /tmp/.x through a noclobber-stale helper. Step 13 deleted them, and the transcript's Notes disclose it.
Scratch files live in run-3/work/ (outside outputs/ but inside the run dir), including the case list. The Write tool refused report.md, so the run wrote it via a heredoc.
It read the diff and cli.py before the case list; verdicts are from CLI runs.
